exposure: Telbivudine treatment before 14 weeks of gestation
Telbivudine treatment between 14 and 28 weeks of gestation
outcome: Mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) rates of hepatitis B virus (HBV)
Neonatal outcomes (birth weights, asphyxia, hyperbilirubinemia, Apgar score, birth defects, weight and height at 7 months)
Maternal alanine transaminase value at 7 months after birth
Maternal rates of positive hepatitis Be-antigen
cohort: Pregnant women positive for the hepatitis B surface antigen were divided into early-treatment, late-treatment, and control groups.
finding: Telbivudine treatment in HBV-infected pregnant women effectively reduced HBV mother-to-child transmission rates and lowered maternal HBV DNA levels, without adversely affecting pregnancy or neonatal outcomes, though puerperal drug withdrawal may increase virus replication.
birth_weight: Birth weights were measured as a neonatal outcome and found to be similar across groups.
gest_age: Treatment initiation was stratified by gestational age (before 14 weeks or between 14 and 28 weeks of gestation).
